clue.text: A melon is prepared for dessert

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up a melon to serve at the end of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' signals an anagram of A MELON IS. Semolina pudding is a classic British school dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina pudding, made from durum wheat grains boiled in milk, is a sweet course.

clue.text: Noteworthy symbol placed over a letter-heading

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes before it

parts.note: a sign is a symbol

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of letter

explanation.surface: A symbol, perhaps an accent, is printed above the top of a written letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'placed over' puts SIGN above A plus L, the first letter of 'letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal success is a striking, remarkable one, used as an adjective.

clue.text: Forced to embrace a married Parisian lady

indicators.note: one word hugging another holds it inside

parts.note: made someone do something means forced them to

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is pressured into hugging a married man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts A and M inside MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a woman, especially a married one.

clue.text: Youths take note when given clues

indicators.note: the youths take a note in, holding it inside their word

parts.note: lads are young men
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Young men write things down when given hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' puts the note E inside LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leads are hints or pointers given to investigators.

clue.text: Tending to make rail workers turn informer

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
to sing is slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: Caring for someone causes railway staff to grass on colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen, was a British rail workers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing a patient is caring for them, looking after them.

clue.text: Military trainees in school display spirit

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: OTC is the Officers' Training Corps, which trains students for the army

explanation.surface: Cadets at a school put on a show of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Officers' Training Corps is a British university cadet force. 'spirit' looks like courage but means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch whisky is a strong distilled drink.

clue.text: Post first held by feature-writer

parts.note: a column is an upright post or pillar
1ST, abbreviating first, is read with the figure as the letter I

explanation.surface: A newspaper job is first taken by a feature writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job but is a pillar; 1ST is written IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist writes a regular feature in a newspaper.

clue.text: Maligned Italian leader in traditional dress

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TRAD is short for traditional, as in trad jazz
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's dictator

explanation.surface: Mussolini is slandered while wearing national costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' adds to the picture of the leader clothed in national costume and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander them, speak ill of them.

clue.text: Hurried to the Andes, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off to South America's mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals an anagram of THE ANDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastened means went quickly, rushed.

clue.text: Try to restore sacred churchyard

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: restoring something rebuilds it, here rearranging the letters of sacred

explanation.surface: An attempt to renovate a holy cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restore' turns SACRED into DSACRE. God's acre is an old phrase, so the solver must trust the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: God's acre is an old poetic name for a burial ground beside a church.

clue.text: Offers shares in firm producing delivery vehicles

explanation.surface: A company issues stock and turns out vans.
explanation.walkthrough: Milk floats are small electric vans used for doorstep milk deliveries in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A company floats when it first sells stock publicly; floats are also electric milk carts.

clue.text: Provide lavish entertainment, as is only fair

explanation.surface: Throwing a lavish party seems only fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them with celebration; a fete is also an outdoor charity fair.

clue.text: Armenian cities are demolished, despite truce

parts.note: ARM is an abbreviation for Armenian

indicators.note: demolished buildings are knocked down and their pieces jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Towns in Armenia are flattened even though a ceasefire holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are demolished' turns CITIES into ISTICE; 'despite' merely links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a ceasefire agreed between warring sides.

clue.text: Maureen is to employ computer assistant

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: Maureen is going to hire a helper for her computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is the hand-held device that helps one point and click on a computer.

clue.text: Self-satisfied, soft-headed simpleton

indicators.note: the soft letter heads the rest, coming first

parts.note: S is short for soft
a mug is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A complacent, feeble-minded idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means pleased with oneself, complacent.

clue.text: Work on the side to produce liquor

explanation.surface: A sideline job making alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to hold a second, often secret job; moonlight is also a slang term for illicitly distilled liquor, like moonshine.

clue.text: Anything but a good-looker!

parts.note: reads as an ugly person, but means a gaze that does harm rather than good

explanation.surface: A remark about someone far from handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good-looker' suggests beauty; the answer is a look that is bad, a malevolent stare.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a curse believed to be cast by a malicious glance.

clue.text: It's not on to gun down distant relation

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
to gun down is to shoot

explanation.surface: Shooting a far-off relative is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not on' looks like 'unacceptable' but gives OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a branch of a family, a remote descendant.

clue.text: Waste resources to make gardenia develop

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Spilled water helps a garden shrub grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' signals an anagram of GARDENIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is the system of pipes and ditches carrying away waste water.

clue.text: Permanently opposed to evil

explanation.surface: Forever against wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: For good means forever; read literally it means in favour of what is good.

clue.text: A stodgy pudding is no good

explanation.surface: A heavy dessert is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff is a British boiled pudding, as in plum duff; duff is also slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff is a heavy steamed dessert, and as slang an adjective meaning worthless or faulty.

clue.text: Masses of utensils

explanation.surface: Lots of kitchen equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots means large amounts, as in pots of money, and also cooking vessels.

clue.text: Pious novice confronts joyless wayfarer

indicators.note: placed in front of, so the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: PI is slang for pious
L, the learner plate, stands for a novice
grim means joyless, cheerless

explanation.surface: A devout beginner faces a gloomy traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword slang for pious; L is the learner sign on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim journeys to a holy place, a traveller on foot.

clue.text: Father always gets upset by fruit

parts.note: papa is a word for father

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ay, or aye, is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Dad is perpetually annoyed by fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' reverses AY to YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaya is a tropical melon-like fruit.

clue.text: University in the country demands representation

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A university wants representation nationally.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes in STATE. 'representation' looks political but means a sculpted likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted likeness of a person.

clue.text: Even now there's silence

explanation.surface: Even at this moment it is quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means up to this moment; the still of the night is its quietness.

clue.text: Spanish composer needs some after collapse

parts.note: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer
part is some of a whole

explanation.surface: A Spanish musician needs a little help after a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart is to break into pieces, to disintegrate.

clue.text: Everyone needs inner energy to write computer language

indicators.note: the outer word needs another placed inside it

parts.note: all means everyone
go means energy, vigour

explanation.surface: Everybody needs inner vitality to write code.
explanation.definitionFit: ALGOL was an early programming language, short for Algorithmic Language.

clue.text: Dutch house of vivid hue

explanation.surface: A Dutch home painted a bright colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange-Nassau is the royal dynasty of the Netherlands, and orange is a bright colour.

clue.text: Italian monk has to concede that it's perfumed

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar
to grant a point is to concede it

explanation.surface: An Italian friar admits that something smells sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant means sweet-smelling, scented.

clue.text: Dine during effort to get agreement

indicators.note: one action happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A meal in the middle of negotiations secures a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' looks like a time word in the surface but signals one piece sitting inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between states.

clue.text: Finding wild celery takes little time

parts.note: small means little
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tracking down a wild herb doesn't take long.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallage is an old name for the wild form of celery.
